intentAndPurpose.intent: Single-selection control within a mutually-exclusive option group.

rules.name: default
useWhen: standard option in a radio group

rules.name: readOnly
useWhen: display-only, value shown but cannot change

props.name: appearance
props.description: Multi-accent appearance role. Controls border, hover, AND fill tokens. `auto` → secondary stack.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label when there is no visible `label` (or when overriding the visible copy). Maps directly to `aria-label` on the underlying radio control.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: When set, names the control via `aria-labelledby` (e.g. `RadioField` single-option layout where the visible label lives on the field, not on this `Radio`).

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether this option is selected. Selection is owned by the parent **`RadioGroup`** via `value` / `defaultValue` matching this `value`. This prop is accepted for tooling (e.g. Storybook) and is **not** forwarded to the underlying primitive.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test automation id — forwarded to the radio control (`BaseRadio.Root`).

props.name: description
props.description: Supplementary copy below the label row. Maps to `aria-describedby` on the control.

props.name: errorHighlight
props.description: Error-state chrome on the wrapper (from `RadioField` when invalid). Standalone `Radio` does not use `errorHighlight`; use `RadioField` for validation UX.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label beside the control. Maps to `aria-label` when the wrapper is a `div`.

props.name: labelWrapper
props.description: Outer wrapper element. Use `'div'` inside a field composition so the visible label is not nested inside a second `<label>`.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether this radio is read-only (focusable but value cannot change)

codeSnippets.title: Basic Usage
codeSnippets.code:
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from '@oneui/ui';

<RadioGroup value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
  <Radio value="a">Option A</Radio>
  <Radio value="b">Option B</Radio>
</RadioGroup>

interactionBehavior.summary: Radio's dot animates by scaling DOWN: it rests at `scale(2)` and `opacity: 0` when unchecked, so checking shrinks a box-filling shape into the dot while it fades in, and unchecking grows it back out. The circle itself scales UP on press — the opposite direction to Button, which squashes down. The most surprising part of the colour model is that the unchecked stroke and hover tint ignore the `appearance` prop entirely: they follow the parent `<Surface>`'s role (Neutral on the bare page and at the palette extremes), while only the checked fill follows `appearance`. Keyboard is standard radio-group roving with two twists — `Enter` is deliberately swallowed so only `Space` selects, and `Home` / `End` are switched off.
hover: Unchecked, the circle's interior fills with the unchecked role's `--{Role}-Hover` (falling back to `--Neutral-Hover`); checked, both the background AND the border step to `--{Role}-Bold-Hover`.
Which role that hover tint comes from is decided by the resolved parent-surface role, not the `appearance` prop — `appearance="positive"` on the bare page still hovers Neutral.
Both rules are wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck fill behind.
The tint lands inside the 16–24px circle only. There is no separate state-layer element, and the circle's `overflow: hidden` clips the fill to the shape.
Read-only and disabled radios never hover — both set `pointer-events: none` on the control.
press: The whole circle scales UP on press: `scale(1 + --Motion-Tap-Scale-Up / 100)`, i.e. +7% by default. Note this is the opposite direction to Button, which scales DOWN.
Unchecked press tints the interior to `--{Role}-Pressed`; checked press moves both fill and border to `--{Role}-Bold-Pressed`.
Press is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so a touch tap gets the same scale-up and tint a mouse press does.
A brand can remove the squash entirely by setting `--Motion-Tap-Scale-Up` to 0.
focus: Keyboard focus draws the standard two-layer halo: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer ring at `calc(--Stroke-XL + --Focus-Outline-Width)`, so it stays legible inside a tinted `<Surface>`.
The outer ring colour is ALWAYS `--Informative-Bold`, never the appearance role — a `positive` or `negative` radio still focuses informative-blue, per the Figma focus-ring spec.
`:focus-visible` only; `.radio:focus` merely clears the native outline, so a mouse click paints no ring.
`box-shadow` is absent from the transition list, so the halo appears and disappears instantly rather than fading.
A global `[data-force-state="focus"]` ancestor hook forces the halo on for documentation and preview screenshots.
Read-only radios stay focusable (Base UI `readOnly`, not `disabled`), so they can still show the halo even though pointer interaction is blocked.
keyboard: `Space` selects the focused option. `Enter` deliberately does nothing — Base UI's Radio root calls `preventDefault()` on the `Enter` keydown specifically so its button helper cannot turn it into a click.
Arrow keys move between options and wrap around at both ends (Base UI's composite root defaults `loopFocus` to true).

All four arrow keys work regardless of the `orientation` prop: RadioGroup never passes an orientation to the composite, so it stays `'both'`. `orientation` only sets `data-orientation` for the group's flex direction.
`Home` / `End` do nothing — RadioGroup explicitly sets `enableHomeAndEndKeys: false`.
Arrowing SELECTS as it moves: the arrow keydown marks the group as touched, and the newly focused radio then clicks its own hidden input. You cannot arrow past an option without selecting it.
Roving tabindex: only the checked radio is the group's single tab stop, so `Tab` enters and leaves the whole group in one step.
selected: Checked paints both `background-color` and `border-color` with `--{Role}-Bold`, and the inner dot with `--{Role}-Bold-TintedA11y` (falling back to `--{Role}-Bold-High`).

The dot's resting unchecked state is `scale(2)` with `opacity: 0` — box-filling and invisible. Checking scales it DOWN to `scale(1)` as it fades in; unchecking scales it back UP to box size as it fades out.
The indicator is rendered with `keepMounted`, so the element always exists — that is what lets the transition run in both directions instead of only on entry.
Neither transition fires on mount, so an initially-unchecked group loads silently with no flash of a box-sized dot.
Selection is owned by the parent `RadioGroup` via `value` / `defaultValue`. `Radio`'s own `checked` prop is tooling-only and is NOT forwarded to the primitive.
disabled: `disabled` on the item — or on `RadioGroup`, which cascades through context — sets `pointer-events: none` plus `cursor: not-allowed` on the circle and dims the whole row to `--Disabled-Opacity` via the `<label>` wrapper.

Here the `not-allowed` cursor IS observable: the circle is `pointer-events: none`, so the pointer falls through to the `<label>` wrapper, which also declares `not-allowed` and keeps its pointer events. This is unlike a natively `disabled` control (see docs/design/disabled-states.md).
Base UI renders the control as a `<span role="radio">` with `aria-disabled`, not a native disabled input, so it stays in the accessibility tree.

`readOnly` is a separate contract at the control level: `aria-readonly` + `data-readonly`, `cursor: default`, `pointer-events: none`, and the checked fill / unchecked stroke are repainted with the neutral `--{Role}-High` ink instead of the brand `Bold`.

Counter-intuitive: a read-only Radio also receives `data-disabled` on its `<label>` wrapper, and the wrapper never receives `data-readonly` — so the `[data-disabled]:not([data-readonly])` rule matches and a read-only row still dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` and shows `cursor: not-allowed`, despite the control itself rendering the distinct read-only ink.
`errorHighlight` sets `data-invalid` on the wrapper but `Radio.module.css` has no `[data-invalid]` rule at all — nothing is painted. Use `RadioField` when you need visible validation chrome.
touch: Hover tints never apply on touch-only devices; the +7% press scale plus the pressed tint are the whole response to a tap.
The circle is only `--Spacing-4` / `--Spacing-5` / `--Spacing-6` (16 / 20 / 24px) at sizes S / M / L — far below the 44px mobile minimum.
The `<label>` wrapper does extend the hit area across the label and description text, but nothing pads the row to 44px; add your own spacing when you need the mobile touch-target minimum.
